BEZ-235 + MK-8669 is expected to give low synergy because both drugs inhibit mTOR (BEZ-235 also inhibits PI3K). Treat it as a negative-control-style test, with the caveat that vertical combinations of PI3K/mTOR and mTORC1 inhibitors can be additive or mildly synergistic in some lines. | Why this experiment: This is the negative-control-style BEZ-235 + MK-8669 test in MDAMB436, where the predicted mean is lowest (-0.27) and the std is high (1.07), to check whether the vertical-mTOR prediction holds.
GELDANAMYCIN + MK-8669 is an untested pair in LNCAP, the line where BEZ-235 + GELDANAMYCIN scored best, so it tests whether HSP90 inhibition plus a second agent works there without BEZ-235.
The same GELDANAMYCIN + MK-8669 pair in A2058 (PTEN-loss, BRAF-mutant) allows a cross-line comparison against the BEZ-235 + GELDANAMYCIN result of 0.49.

BEZ-235 + MK-8669 is not simply a negative control: in MDAMB436 it gave high nominal synergy (10.5) but low inhibition (50.6), for a joint score of -0.02. The combination may be additive-to-synergistic but not strongly growth-inhibitory. Test it in a PI3K-dependent line (e.g., LNCAP) to see whether the synergy is reproducible. | Why this experiment: Replicates the BEZ-235 + MK-8669 synergy-without-inhibition pattern seen in MDAMB436 in PI3K-lesion LNCAP, testing whether it is reproducible.

BEZ-235 + AZD1775 (WEE1 inhibitor) in LNCAP may give a moderately high joint score because PI3K/mTOR blockade can impair DNA-damage repair and WEE1 inhibition forces replication-stressed cells into mitosis. This is exploratory; the shortlist shows only one cell line. | Why this experiment: Tests whether WEE1 inhibition with PI3K/mTOR blockade is active in LNCAP, which has ATM and ARID1A loss, a hypothesis that has had no tests yet. | Predicted responders: LNCAP

Dinaciclib with a DNA-damaging partner was antagonistic once (CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE + DINACICLIB in MDAMB436, joint -4.10), whereas dinaciclib with BEZ-235 or MK-8669 in LNCAP gave low but non-negative joints (0.057 and 0.036). Deprioritise it relative to PI3K/mTOR pairs on model prediction alone. | Why this experiment: DINACICLIB + OXALIPLATIN in MDAMB436 has high predicted uncertainty and tests whether the weak negative prior holds, given the antagonism seen with the other DNA-damaging partner.
